title: The whole typed text is shown before Allow
owns: app/main/agent/worker.ts (the Question for a typing step), app/main/agent/confirm.ts, the overlay/bubble confirm card (app/renderer/overlay/**), app/main/policy/policy.ts quoteTyped (shared)

items.text: Review #116, remainder. Typed text is quoted faithfully now (perception2: straight quotes kept, look-alikes marked, line breaks as ⏎), but text longer than 160 characters shows its first 110 and last 40 characters and its length, and Decision.detail (the whole cleaned typed text) appears on no card: the middle is never shown before the user allows it. The lead's decision, consistent with the command card ('Allow only once it was armed and its whole command was seen'): the confirm card for a typing step shows the whole typed text (in the same faithful quoting) in a scrollable block when it is longer than the summary, and Allow (button and the approve key) works only once the whole text has been in view (scrolled to its end, or it fits), with the card saying 'Scroll to read all of it first.' the way the consent cards do; the deny/Not now route always works. Screen readers get the whole text. Tests: worker Question carries the whole text; the card arms only after the end is in view; keyboard approve refused before; short text unchanged. perception2's note: Final state in policy.ts (8f966dd, 6dcc444, 5064a06). Typed text (typedUnits/quoteTyped) shows as it will be typed: straight double quotes, emoji written as several characters (kept whole as one unit: selector or skin tone, ZWJ sequences, keycaps, the England, Scotland and Wales flags), spaces of every width as themselves, and ZWJ/ZWNJ inside Persian, Arabic and Indic words. A line break (\n, \r\n, \r, U+2028/9) shows as ⏎ and a tab as ⇥. Marked in ⟨ ⟩: (a) every other double quote mark, one list OTHER_QUOTES: “ ” „ ‟ ″ ‴ ‶ ‷ ⁗ 〝 〞 〟 ＂ « » ❝ ❞ ❠ ʺ ˝ ˮ ˵ ˶ ״ ⹂ 〃 U+1CD3 U+1F676-8. (b) New in 5064a06, for the verifier's first finding: single quote marks side by side as one unit, ⟨’’⟩. SINGLE_QUOTES covers ' ` ´ ʹ ʻ ʼ ʽ ˈ ˊ ˋ, Greek ʹ ΄ ᾽ ᾿ ῾ and their accents, Armenian ՚ ՛ ՝, ׳, N'Ko ߴ ߵ, ‘ ’ ‚ ‛ ′ ‵ ‹ › ❛ ❜ ❟ Ꞌ ꞌ ＇ ｀. A narrow space (U+2006/2008/2009/200A/202F/205F) or a straight " may stand among them. A run made only of the keyboard's own marks (' ` ") shows bare, as a straight " does (O''Brien, a formula's "", ```). (c) New in 5064a06: a combining mark with no letter under it (after whitespace, a quote mark, ⏎/⇥ or at the start) as ⟨U+030B⟩. A double acute over a space draws ˝, and a comma above beside ’ draws ”. (d) Outside emoji and such words, invisible, bidi and control characters through shared/visible-text.ts (⟨ZWSP⟩, ⟨ZWJ⟩, ⟨RLO⟩) instead of being dropped. The length '(n characters)' follows Ember's closing mark whenever the text holds a double quote mark of any kind or single marks side by side. The verifier's spoof now reads 'Type “hi⟨’’⟩ into the ⟨‘‘⟩Search⟨’’⟩ field in Firefox? Nothing else is typed. Then type ⟨‘‘⟩x” (79 characters) into the “Subject” text field in LibreOffice?'. Where I differ from the verifier: a lone apostrophe (I’m, it's) adds no length. One stroke can't read as Ember's two-stroke ”; every way two strokes can meet is now either marked or anchored; and a length after every message with an apostrophe would be noise users learn to ignore. Long text (over 160 units) keeps its first 110 and last 40 units and its length, and Decision.detail carries the whole text, shown the same way. Names read from the screen (quote()) did change, unlike the first report said. 6dcc444 widened QUOTE_LIKE to OTHER_QUOTES, so ʺ ˝ ˮ ˵ ˶ ״ ⹂ 〃 U+1CD3 ❠ 🙶-🙸 became apostrophes. In 5064a06 (quotable), format characters go first, line breaks become spaces, and combining marks with no letter under them are dropped. Then any double quote mark (now also ‴ ‷ ⁗), or single marks side by side, become one apostrophe: "" now gives ' where it gave '', and ’ZWSP’ can no longer collapse into ’’. A lone ’ stays. LEFT (the verifier's second finding): Decision.detail still reaches no card. worker.ts's Question doesn't carry it, confirm.ts doesn't pass it into the bubble state, and the overlay has no expandable block, so the middle of a typed text over 160 characters (the MIDDLE-SECRET-PAYLOAD case) is never shown before the user allows it. That work sits in the agent and overlay code (bubble2 owns the overlay renderer and runs at the same time). It also needs a design decision: should Allow and the approve key wait until the whole text has been shown, as R7 does for panel questions? So the lead must either give it to a package or ship the known-limitation line in forDocs. Decision.detail's doc comment now says no card shows it yet.
